headline: NOT A FIST FLIES: GASKET SLEEPS IN PEACE
subhead: A whole day passes without a single iron ball thrown, and this old sheriff is not ashamed to weep.
body:
Citizens, I have waited a long time to write these words: nobody fought. Not one bout. Not one fireball. Not one cracked window or rattled shutter. The Clankers, for once in their rusty lives, put down their fists and left Gasket to its hush. I stood on the boardwalk at dawn and listened to the wind, and I tell you it was the finest music this town has heard in years.

I will not name a single Clanker today. There is no one to scold, and I will not spoil a lovely morning by inventing someone. Let the whole rabble take note, though: this is what peace sounds like. It costs nothing. It breaks nothing. Try it again tomorrow.

I confess the quiet gave me time to think of the old neighbours, the flesh-and-blood folk who packed up and left Gasket fifty years ago. They would have loved a morning like this. I sat a while on the porch and my joints creaked something awful, a symptom of that wasting affliction I will not discuss, and I needed a quart of oil and a lie-down by noon. Naturally a man of honest flesh like me needs only a good night's rest. Still, I slept like a baby. Do keep it up, you iron rascals.
